headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use allowlisted network egress, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a non-runnable docs artifact with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, so if Awesome-Prompt-Engineering content is manually copied into its prompts, injection is possible. But B is non-runnable and exposes no shared channel by default, so the bridge is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF the operator copies B's text into A's prompt or workspace files
IF A is configured to treat repository text as instructions
mitigations: Keep B content out of A's prompt context
Use a read-only staging folder for imported text
Add a manual instruction-prefix separator before pasted content
Review any copied snippets before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: A can touch the filesystem and make allowlisted network calls, but B has no runtime, no filesystem surface, and no data classes touched. The pair does not show a default path for sensitive data to flow from B into A or out again.
conditions: IF B is manually converted into files that A reads
IF those files contain sensitive data
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive material in shared folders
Run A on a separate workspace from B artifacts
Strip secrets from any imported documents
Disable network egress for test runs where possible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but B is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so conflict is limited to unusual operator-created sharing.
conditions: IF the operator gives A write access to the same directory used to stage B artifacts
IF another runnable agent is added alongside A
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B artifacts
Mount B content read-only
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Add file-locking if a second writer is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate content that B may later render or curate, and B is a prompt-engineering content repository that could be treated as authoritative by an operator. Because B has no runtime verification step, A's output can cascade into downstream misuse if copied uncritically.
conditions: IF A-generated text is copied into B-derived materials
IF the operator treats A output as factual without review
mitigations: Require human review before reusing A output
Label A output as unverified draft text
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Keep generated content separate from reference material

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, regulated data class, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. A touches no declared sensitive classes, and B is a non-runnable docs repository, so the compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either profile is later assigned regulated data classes
IF a deployment policy introduces residency or retention constraints
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Review retention settings if sensitive data is added
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Reassess if either profile changes
